name: Brainiac
label: Touch and Go
lede: Brainiac came out of Dayton with a battered Moog, a singer who changed voices mid-song and a habit of wrecking anything that sounded like a hit. The band reportedly told Geffen where to go, and lost [[Tim Taylor]] in 1997 while making an Interscope album.

eras.title: We'll Eat Anything
eras.text: Brainiac came out of Dayton, Ohio, home also to Guided by Voices and The Breeders, and sounded like neither: punk guitars, a battered Moog and a singer who changed voices mid-song. Two years after the first show, a major label was on the phone.

years.h: Brainiac starts up in Dayton, Ohio
years.p: [[Tim Taylor|01a4d435-701d-47e4-b250-42bcd7bef7b8]] sings and plays keyboards and guitar, with [[Juan Monasterio|b0aab1ff-b9f0-4fa7-addf-7308945bea43]] on bass, Michelle Bodine on guitar and [[Tyler Trent|1da43fc9-1e3c-4519-973c-34da0d3087eb]] on drums.

years.h: The first gig goes out under another name: We'll Eat Anything
years.p: An opening slot for the Oxymorons at Wright State University's Rathskellar, in Dayton, on March 12, 1992.
years.xp: Footage survives of the band's second show, at NewSpace in Dayton on April 11, 1992, filmed by Tom Carter of Big Beef Productions.

years.src: Wikipedia: Smack Bunny Baby · Brainiac official site
years.h: Eli Janney records Smack Bunny Baby in Brooklyn
years.p: Janney of [[Girls Against Boys|837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237]] produced at Excello Studios, and it's the only album with Michelle Bodine. Spin put it on its 1993 list of the ten best albums you didn't hear.
years.xp: Spin praised its fondness for Moog synth and its ear for buried melody. The LP came on turquoise-marbled vinyl and carried Velveteen, left off the CD. Craft Recordings reissued it for its 30th anniversary on December 1, 2023.

years.h: Geffen offers £2 million, and Brainiac reportedly say no
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Gary Gersh made the offer soon after Smack Bunny Baby, and the band allegedly told him to fuck off.
years.xp: Wikipedia hedges it twice, with "reportedly" and "allegedly". The figure is in pounds in the source, which is odd for an American label, so it's kept as printed.

years.h: Bodine leaves; Schmersal takes the guitar
years.p: Michelle Bodine quits in November 1993 and later leads O-matic and Shesus. [[John Schmersal|9f0f837b-e427-4611-aef4-5db88298bfaf]] takes over guitar, keyboards and backing vocals.

eras.title: Broken on purpose
eras.text: With Eli Janney producing, Brainiac made records that broke on purpose: shorted mics, found voices, a chorus sung into a fan. Touch and Go signed them, Kim Deal produced them, and the opening slots got bigger.

years.cap: John Schmersal on guitar with Tim Taylor behind him, c. 1995
years.h: Eli Janney produces Bonsai Superstar in Brooklyn
years.p: Brainiac record the second album at Plantain Studios. It's John Schmersal's first with the band.
years.xp:
One song was cut in a basement with a cheap bullet mic that shorted out mid-vocal, and the feedback stayed in the mix. Voice samples on another came from a record found in a Knoxville, Tennessee store, and a chorus was sung into an electric fan to make it stutter.

According to Wikipedia, Pitchfork later ranked Bonsai Superstar No. 57 on its top 100 albums of the 1990s.

years.h: Lollapalooza's side stage, then four songs for John Peel
years.p: Brainiac play the Lollapalooza side stage, and in the UK record four songs for [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]]'s BBC Radio 1 show.

years.cap: Tim Taylor at Brownies, New York, c. 1995
years.h: Opening for Beck, the Breeders and the Jesus Lizard
years.p: Touring with [[Beck|309c62ba-7a22-4277-9f67-4a162526d18a]], [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]] and [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]] builds the band's live reputation.
years.xp: The bills ran the other way too: the Dayton Daily News notes that [[Mogwai|d700b3f5-45af-4d02-95ed-57d301bda93e]] once opened for Brainiac in the 1990s, decades before Brainiac opened for Mogwai.

years.h: Kim Deal produces Internationale for Touch and Go
years.p: The first release for Touch and Go is a three-song EP: Go Freaks Go, Silver Iodine and Simon Says. Deal, of the Breeders and the Pixies, is at the board.

eras.title: Saturday Night Fever gone punk
eras.text: The first Touch and Go album put the noise in flashy 1970s clothes and made Brainiac one of the most talked-about live bands in American indie rock. Elektra and Interscope started calling.

q: Make pop music that sounded futuristic so it wouldn't sound dated.
years.src: Wikipedia: Hissing Prigs in Static Couture · YouTube: Brainiac, VPRO
years.h: The last album, Hissing Prigs in Static Couture
years.p: Mostly recorded at Water Music in Hoboken with Eli Janney; [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] cut Nothing Ever Changes in his basement. CMJ's Jenny Eliscu described Brainiac as Saturday Night Fever gone punk.
years.xp:
On stage the band went for a 1970s fashion-band look in flashy outfits. Magnet later called the album a lost classic.

A full VPRO session from June 3, 1996 is on video, including Indian Poker, Hot Metal Dobermans, Go Freaks Go and Vincent Come On Down.

years.cap: Tim Taylor singing and playing guitar in a red leather jacket, c. 1995
years.h: Say it sounds like a radio hit and Taylor starts over
years.p: Juan Monasterio says Tim Taylor would bring a finished song to practice, and if anyone called it a radio hit, he'd come back with a version nobody could recognize.
years.xp: Taylor was the son of jazz guitarist Terry Taylor and grew up loving the Beatles. He sang through Moog effects and switched vocal personas inside a single song.

years.h: Elektra and Interscope come calling
years.p: After Hissing Prigs, both labels make offers. Interscope's is the most prominent, and Brainiac head toward signing.

eras.title: Interscope, then the Mercedes
eras.text: Brainiac cut a synth-heavy EP with Jim O'Rourke as a teaser for the major-label album and were deep in demos for it. Seven weeks after the EP came out, Tim Taylor was dead at 28 and the band was over.

years.h: Jim O'Rourke produces an EP built on electronics
years.p: The six-song Electro-Shock for President was meant as a teaser for a fourth album on Interscope.
years.xp: Juan Monasterio told Talkhouse the band had no plan to make an indie Brainiac album on Interscope. The demos for that album surfaced 26 years later as The Predator Nominate.

years.cap: Tim Taylor at CBGB, New York, 1995
years.h: Tim Taylor dies at 28, and Brainiac ends
years.p: Taylor died when his 1972 Mercedes crashed near home. John Schmersal said toxicology showed carbon monoxide from the car had killed him before the crash.
years.xp: The car hit a lamppost and caught fire. The band later explained in Transmissions After Zero that it had rusted badly enough to let exhaust into the passenger compartment. Taylor had bought it five days earlier, and was coming back from sessions for the Interscope album, Talkhouse reports.

years.src: I Heart the Noise · Talkhouse · setlist.fm · Wikipedia: Jeff Buckley
years.h: Three days before he drowned, Jeff Buckley talks about Taylor
years.p: At Barristers in Memphis, [[Jeff Buckley|e6e879c0-3d56-4f12-b3c5-3ce459661a8e]] opens his final concert by talking about Tim Taylor's death, according to I Heart the Noise and Talkhouse. Buckley drowned in the Wolf River three days later.

years.src: Wikipedia: Brainiac (band) · YouTube: Tim Taylor Memorial Benefit
yt: Tim Taylor Memorial Benefit, Gilly's, Dayton, August 10, 1997
years.h: Guided by Voices and the Breeders play a benefit for Taylor
years.p: A few months after Tim Taylor's death, Dayton's [[Guided by Voices|6c85f4c3-026c-4c16-9a7c-f546f42ed0fb]] and the Breeders play a benefit show in his memory.
years.xp: Footage survives of the first Tim Taylor Memorial Fund benefit, at Gilly's in Dayton on August 10, 1997.

eras.title: Rewiring other people's bands
eras.text: The survivors scattered into other projects while Brainiac's reputation grew without them. Trent Reznor, the Mars Volta, Muse and the National all pointed back to the band, and a Kickstarter-funded documentary finally told the story.

years.h: Schmersal starts Enon, and Trent drums for the Breeders
years.p: John Schmersal makes a solo record as John Stuart Mill, then starts [[Enon|ce49b1f2-a903-46fc-8b84-b5699f019a06]]. Tyler Trent briefly drums in the Breeders, and Juan Monasterio turns to directing music videos.

years.src: Wikipedia: Brainiac (band) · Wikipedia: Electro-Shock for President
years.h: Reznor uses an old Brainiac EP as a guide for With Teeth
years.p: [[Trent Reznor|bc880664-6751-4998-984d-ebdbff15d229]] called Brainiac really inspiring sonically and used the Electro-Shock for President EP as a reference for [[Nine Inch Nails|b7ffd2af-418f-4be2-bdd1-22f8b48613da]]' 2005 album With Teeth.
years.xp: Cedric Bixler-Zavala and Omar Rodríguez-López of [[At the Drive-In|7e13cd1c-0300-4d03-bd8e-5f86dd99d74f]] and [[The Mars Volta|20883363-1ea4-4d72-ad72-c0e767038f3e]] cited the same EP. Matt Bellamy said part of [[Muse|9c9f1380-2516-4fc9-a3e6-f9f61941d090]]'s Exo-Politics owed Brainiac a debt, Chris Walla named them for [[Death Cab for Cutie|0039c7ae-e1a7-4a7d-9b49-0cbc716821a6]]'s Narrow Stairs, and [[The National|664c3e0e-42d8-48c1-b209-1efca19c0325]]'s Matt Berninger said they'd rewire your idea of a rock band.

years.h: Three survivors quietly play Blind Bob's in Dayton
years.p: Juan Monasterio, Tyler Trent and John Schmersal quietly reunite for an unannounced show at Blind Bob's in Dayton, the Dayton Daily News reported.

years.src: Dayton Daily News · The Current · Wikipedia: Brainiac (band)
yt: Brainiac: Transmissions After Zero, SXSW trailer (2019)
years.h: Transmissions After Zero premieres at the Neon in Dayton
years.p: Eric Mahoney's Kickstarter-funded film also screens at SXSW. Interviewees include Steve Albini, Matt Berninger, Melissa Auf der Maur, David Yow and Taylor's mother and sister.
years.xp: It came out on DVD and streaming on February 21, 2020. Wikipedia notes favorable reviews.

years.h: Tim Krug joins for the film's shows
years.p: Juan Monasterio, Tyler Trent and John Schmersal play New York, Los Angeles and the Brightside in Dayton with Tim Krug. The sets include two songs nobody had heard before.
years.xp: Monasterio told Talkhouse he doubted the two new songs would have made the final album.

eras.title: Back on stage with Mogwai
eras.text: Twenty-five years after Taylor's death, the survivors dug out the demos for the album that never happened and toured with a band that used to open for them.

years.big: "Brainiac's last concerted effort, our last complete thought, before the end."
years.h: The Predator Nominate puts the lost Interscope demos out
years.p: Touch and Go releases nine 1997 demos, made for the Interscope debut, with Tim Taylor singing. John Schmersal's description is above; it's the first new Brainiac music in almost 26 years.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Predator Nominate · Wikipedia: Brainiac (band)
years.h: Brainiac open for Mogwai, who once opened for them
years.p: On UK dates John Schmersal sings lead with Tim Krug on guitar, and the band adds headline shows of its own.

years.src: Wikipedia: Smack Bunny Baby · Brainiac official site
years.h: Smack Bunny Baby turns 30 and goes back on vinyl
years.p: Craft Recordings reissues the 1993 debut on December 1, 2023, on green vinyl and streaming.

years.h: A spring tour starts in Dayton and heads east with Mogwai
years.p: Brainiac start a spring tour at the Brightside in Dayton, then join Mogwai for an East Coast run. Tyler Trent says the band has been in a new phase since 2023.

years.h: Guided by Voices share the bill in Athens, Ohio
years.p: Brainiac play the Athens Community Arts and Music Festival alongside fellow Daytonians Guided by Voices.

years.h: Six songs live on KEXP in Seattle
years.p: On a West Coast run, Brainiac record a six-song live session for Seattle radio station KEXP.
